God I hate to break it to you but the .30-06 is just a 10 mm longer .308 Winchester. They both shoot a .308 diameter bullet. They both shoot a 150 grain .308 projectile at 2800 FPS. The ballistics are the same up until about 180 grain projectiles. After that the longer case of the .30-06 allow you to shoot a slower burning powder that keeps chamber pressures in a safe range. (55,000 psi or so). As for being less expensive with factory ammo its a wash. Of course if you are shooting government surplus you will find it cheaper but then again it is not .308 Winchester but 7.62X51 NATO with some minor different characteristics. Some military 7.62 NATO rifles may have a little longer chamber than a .308 Winchester (Clint Mckee has written extensively about this) However that being said you can shoot government surplus 7.62 NATO in commercial .308 rifles which out any problems. The NATO brass may be a little softer than commercial brass so you might not get as many reloads out of it.

The difference in accuracy unless you are shooting a very highly tuned target rifle is almost negligible and certainly beyond the capabilities of most but championship shooters.
